arguments.premise_synthesis: Real median household income has generally trended upward over time, albeit with dips after 2008 and 2019; this rising income means that the debt service burden for typical households is not increasing, even as nominal debt levels rise.
arguments.conclusion_supported: It establishes that rising real median household income helps keep household debt service manageable, reducing the likelihood of a household-driven economic collapse and supporting the broader claim that a crash is not imminent.
